ideas.title: Product Management in the Age of Fast
ideas.statement: AI made building dramatically faster and cheaper — but it did not make governing what gets built any easier, and the gap between the two is where organizations now fail.

connections.note: The speed-era governance argument builds on the observation that AI changed the economics of building software — cheaper, faster execution is exactly what resets organizational expectations.

incomingConnections.note: Cheaper, AI-assisted testing widens the gap between running experiments and learning from them — the compounding argument starts where the speed argument ends.

ideas.title: The Cost of AI
ideas.statement: The force reshaping organizations is not only what AI can do — it is what AI costs: a distributed, largely ungoverned expense that stays invisible until finance connects the dots.

incomingConnections.note: The speed-era governance argument builds on the observation that AI changed the economics of building software — cheaper, faster execution is exactly what resets organizational expectations.

ideas.title: Definition-First
ideas.statement: Clarity earns a product its existence. A product should be able to say precisely what it is for and who it is for; when it cannot, that absence — not a missing feature — is the signal to question whether it should exist at all.

incomingConnections.note: Definition-first argues clarity earns a product its existence. Portfolio Dynamics applies that same standard to the exit side and to portfolio scope, where almost nobody applies it — the same discipline pointed at a different moment in a product's life.

ideas.title: Experimentation That Compounds
ideas.statement: Experimentation only becomes an advantage when platform, program, and culture work together to turn individual test results into institutional knowledge — organizations that merely run tests do not compound.

connections.note: Cheaper, AI-assisted testing widens the gap between running experiments and learning from them — the compounding argument starts where the speed argument ends.

ideas.title: Portfolio Dynamics
ideas.statement: Product portfolios are not designed as much as they are accumulated. They are the visible result of thousands of individually rational decisions made over time. This idea explores why that accumulation becomes difficult to reverse—and why healthier portfolios begin with better decision systems, not better cleanup.

connections.note: Definition-first argues clarity earns a product its existence. Portfolio Dynamics applies that same standard to the exit side and to portfolio scope, where almost nobody applies it — the same discipline pointed at a different moment in a product's life.

artifacts.title: The Secret Force Behind AI-Driven Workforce Decisions.
artifacts.deck: What if the secret force pushing organizations to adapt its workforce isn't AI's ability to replace people but the cost of AI itself?

artifacts.title: Product Management in the Age of Fast. What Speed Actually Changed.
artifacts.deck: If AI can move faster than our processes, are product management rituals and governance gates still necessary?

incomingRelationships.note: Develops the expectation problem created by the speed shift described in the earlier piece: organizations generalize the easy cases.

artifacts.title: Product Management in the Age of Fast. The Expectation Problem.
artifacts.deck: Organizations are taking the cases where building got easier and generalizing the feeling across all deliveries.

relationships.note: Develops the expectation problem created by the speed shift described in the earlier piece: organizations generalize the easy cases.

artifacts.title: Experimentation Platforms Are Becoming Organizational Memory
artifacts.deck: Documentation keeps conclusions and loses the reasoning behind them. Experimentation platforms keep the reasoning, which quietly makes them the place an organization stores what it knows.

relationships.note: Picks up where that piece ended — the difference between running experiments and building knowledge — and argues the experimentation platform is where the compounding record actually lives.

incomingRelationships.note: Takes that piece's claim — the platform's real output is preserved reasoning — and shows what the lost reasoning costs: it is what caps a program at ten experiments a quarter.

artifacts.title: From First Hypothesis to Institutional Knowledge
artifacts.deck: What best-in-class experimentation actually looks like. And why platform, program, and culture must work together.

incomingRelationships.note: Picks up where that piece ended — the difference between running experiments and building knowledge — and argues the experimentation platform is where the compounding record actually lives.

Extends its argument that cheaper experiments only widen the gap between programs that keep knowledge and those that lose it, by tracing the mechanism to the specific costs memory removes from each test.

artifacts.title: Learning Is the Product
artifacts.deck: Experiment volume looks like a staffing number. Take it apart and most of it is knowledge the program produced and lost.

artifacts.title: Portfolio Rationalization Is an Operating System Problem
artifacts.deck: Healthy portfolios aren't the product of periodic cleanups but of operating systems — funding, governance, cadence, ownership, and incentives — that question continuation as rigorously as they question entry.

relationships.note: Turns the entry/continuation asymmetry into a prescription: if accumulation is produced by the operating model, that is where the fix has to live.

artifacts.title: The Decision That Could Wait
artifacts.deck: Products are subjected to rigorous scrutiny before they enter a portfolio. Far fewer organizations apply that same scrutiny to keeping them there.

relationships.note: Takes the observation that portfolios accumulate rather than get designed and locates the mechanism behind it: entry is scrutinized, continuation is not.

incomingRelationships.note: Turns the entry/continuation asymmetry into a prescription: if accumulation is produced by the operating model, that is where the fix has to live.

artifacts.title: The Portfolio Nobody Designed
artifacts.deck: Portfolios aren't built. They accumulate through hundreds of decisions that make perfect sense in isolation but collectively create complexity nobody set out to build.

incomingRelationships.note: Takes the observation that portfolios accumulate rather than get designed and locates the mechanism behind it: entry is scrutinized, continuation is not.
